basis: Rule 2: no sized findings; items 0-2 are outside the window and 3-7 are null searches, with the price pinned by a fixed US$5.214 cash offer.
against: A Genel counter-bid or deal-break news (items 1-2) could move it, but nothing is dated inside the window.

basis: Item 0: an ex-dividend of about 1.9% of spot lands in the same session and the resolver reads unadjusted closes; it is a single mechanical item, so rules 1 and 8 cap a short below 5 at 35, and rule 9 does not apply because the median reaction is 1.5%.
against: The drop is mechanical and small; a clean H1 with the Edison rent-haircut release (item 2) could offset it, and past ex-dates were sometimes positive.

basis: Rule 6 (bar too high): under its stated conservative method the company's first FY27 EBITDA guide is likely well below the EUR 266m consensus (item 0), partly offset by a possible dividend reinstatement (item 1); a short below 5 stays at 35 or below (rule 8).
against: The stock already trades at a deep discount to consensus targets, so a low guide may be priced; guide-day reactions have run 6-15% either way.

basis: Item 0: H2 revenue consensus implies a decline against July +23.9% and the largest competitor in administration, so an outlook raise is likely; rule 6 halves 'beats a low bar' and caps it at 35, partly offset by profit-conversion risk (item 1).
against: Item 1: a history of profit shortfalls despite revenue growth (Nov-25, -12.5%), and a +10.8% 20-day run-up after the Headlam news is partly priced.

basis: Items 0-1: production running above the 34-42 kboepd range and an FCF upgrade on Brent; rule 6 halves this low-bar case, rule 4 discounts the Brent proxy, and the moderate 2.45% short is not crowded.
against: The last FCF upgrade was sold off (-6.66%), and Brent fell about 7% on the eve of the window.

basis: Item 0: BizLink monthly revenue is a supplier proxy with peer read-across (rules 4 and 5); items 1-2 are a weak absence-of-filing negative and a vol-compression argument with no direction, so the sum is small.
against: Item 1: no pre-announcement this quarter, unlike February, hints there is no large beat, and +7.3 put skew with a 14% median reaction makes either tail large.

basis: Item 1 (a new director's open-market buy) is the only primary long item; item 0 (job postings) is a proxy under rule 4, and item 2 (out-of-the-money Fit warrants) offsets them.
against: Item 2: the Fit CEPA's stalled optionality, plus heavy dilution and an 11.6-point put skew.

basis: Item 1 (bar too high, rule 6): the first FY27 EPS guide sits on about 9-10% more shares, after a prior guide cut for the same reason; item 0 is the deal-announcement reaction pattern and item 2 is ambiguous; a short below 5 is capped and the stock rose into the print (rule 8, -5).
against: Upside skew of -17.1 shows strong call demand, and the read-across from peers (OKTA, FTNT) was positive.

basis: Rule 3: more than 22% of float is short, alongside a 3%-a-quarter buyback (item 1, 10-Q) and an AI seat tier in the live API (item 0); items 3-4 net small negatives, and the crowded short adds certainty to the long.
against: Items 3-4: three finance-leadership changes in six months and the price above the average target with no estimate slack after a +16% run-up; peer item 2 carries no weight.

basis: Item 1: covenant headroom is tight as a strong quarter rolls out of LTM (primary document); item 0 is a Hormuz macro proxy, which rule 4 makes anti-informative; a short below 5 stays low.
against: JELD-WEN raised guidance (item 6), and the stock is already down 10% over 20 days.

basis: Items 0-2 are industry and macro proxies (storage installs, office vacancy, airline costs) under rule 4; item 3, from the 10-Q, removes a self-insurance left tail; the net sum is small.
against: The last three of four Q3/Q2-type prints fell 8-9%, and the proxy items carry no company-level confirmation.

basis: Rules 1 and 7: at least three same-direction primary-document items, a Q4 guide implying a 15-25% YoY decline (item 0), a harvest-mode strategy change (item 1), and a $200m shelf on a $23.5m float with a super-voting bump and a Nasdaq minimum-bid clock (item 4), stacked on a microcap with no crowded short.
against: The stock rose about 12% into the print (rule 8, -5); with no options and a thin float a squeeze is possible, and the company has guided before.

basis: Items 0-1 are tariff-rate and refund windfall themes, which rule 5 gives no weight; item 2 (a back-half-loaded plan under a new CFO, bar too high) roughly cancels them.
against: A guide raise built on lower tariffs could produce a large up-move; this is a correlated tariff theme across many retailers.

basis: Items 0-2: the 53-week-year comparison and a guide set late in the quarter narrow the downside; rule 6 halves this low-bar case, and peer La-Z-Boy (item 3, rule 5) points the other way.
against: Six of the last seven prints fell, and one covering analyst at $0.44 GAAP leaves room for a headline mismatch.

basis: Item 0: no 8-K backs the H2 inorganic bridge (bar too high, rule 6); item 3: a 10% holder is selling daily; item 2: the run-up rests on a product launch; offset by insider buying at $3.25 (item 4); a short below 5 that rose into the print is capped (rule 8, -5).
against: Item 4: insiders bought at $3.25 and removal of going-concern language is possible; analysts unanimously rate it Buy.

basis: Item 1: the reaffirmed FY27 target is arithmetically out of reach (bar too high, rule 6); item 3: covenant waiver history and a tightening ratio (distress, rule 7, single item); the MSA peer item carries no weight; the deferred gain (item 0) offsets.
against: Item 0: the deferred divestiture gain could produce a headline EPS beat against the -$0.05 single estimate.

basis: Item 0: a fresh Form 144 brings the IFC seller back into the print week; item 1: the profitability claim hinges on Q4 clearing a goodwill test, with a history of restatements; a short below 5 stays capped.
against: Item 2 is two-sided (the first three-year outlook could reassure), and the median reaction is only 2.5%.

basis: Items 0 and 13: the guide implies flat sequential revenue against +9% last year; rule 6 halves this low-bar case and caps it at 35; items 1 and 12 rest on airfare CPI, a proxy under rule 4.
against: Take-rate compression (item 1's downside half) and continuing insider supply; consensus at the guide midpoint is common and is not evidence of a beat.

basis: Item 0: a two-analyst consensus below the peer-implied rate arithmetic (peer read-across plus a low bar, rules 5 and 6 halve it), with spot rates as a proxy (item 3); drydock off-hire (item 1) and no September dividend (item 2) offset.
against: Five drydockings in Q2 and seven in Q3 hit utilisation, and the stock is up 14% into the print near its 52-week high.

basis: Item 1: Q2 is the company's own seasonal S&M-ratio trough, documented in its releases, and the last Q2 print fell 11.5%; WDH's channel-cost bid (item 0) is peer read-across and the regulation (item 2) takes effect after the print; a short below 5 is capped.
against: Item 3: segment demand is accelerating (+15% P&C health premiums, WDH insurance income +80%), and up-moves dominate this name's history.

basis: Items 0-1 (bar too high, rule 6): the FY delivery target needs a record Q4, and the company has printed at or below the bottom of its guides twice; item 2 is a macro rate proxy; rule 3 caps the short at 20 because item 3 documents about 8.5% of float short and building.
against: Item 3: 8.5% of float short and rising, a sequential margin inflection confirmed by a peer, and call-rich skew near the 52-week low; under rule 3 shorts against this were 0 of 3.
